If you've initialized all elements of `predecessors` to `-1` (which is a common practice to indicate that a node has not been visited yet), then using `n != -1` makes sense because it checks if the current node has a predecessor (i.e., it has been visited).

However, if you've initialized `predecessors` to some other value (e.g., `0`), then using `n >= 0` would be more appropriate because it checks if the current node has a non-negative predecessor.

In general, it's a good practice to initialize your vectors to a value that makes sense for your algorithm and to use that value in your conditions. This can help avoid confusion and make your code more readable.
